title: Pain in Parkinson's
content: Pain can occur in people with Parkinson's disease and may have different causes. Muscle stiffness, rigidity, changes in posture, reduced movement and other musculoskeletal problems can contribute to discomfort or pain. Some people may also experience nerve-related or other types of pain. Pain should not automatically be assumed to be caused by Parkinson's disease because many other conditions can cause it. The location, severity, duration and circumstances of pain are important when determining its possible cause. New, severe, persistent or worsening pain should be discussed with an appropriate healthcare professional.
